intro.t: Part 4 is your chance to sound like an adult. Give your opinion, support it, show the other side, then bring it home. Six frames, one complete answer.

close.t: Excellent. Opinion, reason, example, the other side, and a clear ending. That's a complete Part 4 answer.

minute.title: Now a whole answer.
crib: Having said that, some people argue that…
So, on the whole, I'd say…
What do you think, Tomás? I agree with what Inês said about…

parts.t: Personally, I think that it's a brilliant idea. The main reason is that nobody teaches us how to save. For example, lots of young people spend their first salary in a week. Having said that, some people argue that parents should teach this at home. So, on the whole, I'd say schools should do it, because not every family can. What do you think, Inês?

minute.q: Should young people learn how to manage money at school?

reels.note: Answer the question in your first sentence.

ex.t: {Personally, I think that} phones should be banned during lessons, but not at break.

ex.q: Is it better to grow up in a city or a small town?
ex.t: {Personally, I think that} a small town is better for young children.

ex.q: Will robots do most jobs in the future?
ex.t: {Personally, I think that} robots will do the boring jobs, but not the creative ones.

reels.note: One clear reason beats three vague ones.

ex.t: Yes, they should. {The main reason is that} it teaches you the value of money.

ex.q: Is online learning as good as learning in a classroom?
ex.t: Not really. {The main reason is that} it's hard to stay focused at home.

ex.q: Should sport be compulsory at school?
ex.t: I think so. {The main reason is that} many teenagers never exercise otherwise.

reels.note: A real example from your life is worth a lot.

ex.q: Is fast fashion a problem we should care about?
ex.t: It is. {For example,} a cheap T-shirt can travel across the world before you buy it.

ex.q: Do you think technology makes people lazy?
ex.t: Sometimes. {For example,} we take the lift even to go up one floor.

ex.q: Is social media good or bad for friendships?
ex.t: Both. {For example,} I talk to my cousin in Canada every week, but I rarely call my friends here.

reels.p: Having said that, some people argue that …
reels.bt: Having said that, some people argue that…
reels.note: Examiners love it: it proves you can see both sides.

ex.t: I'd love less homework. {Having said that, some people argue that} it helps you remember what you've learned.

ex.q: Are video games a waste of time?
ex.t: Not always. {Having said that, some people argue that} they can be addictive.

ex.q: Is tourism good or bad for places like islands?
ex.t: It brings money. {Having said that, some people argue that} it makes everything more expensive for local people.

reels.p: So, on the whole, I'd say …
reels.bt: So, on the whole, I'd say…
reels.note: Return to your answer, in one sentence.

ex.q: Should public transport be free for teenagers?
ex.t: {So, on the whole, I'd say} yes, because it helps families and the planet.

ex.q: Is it better to study alone or with friends?
ex.t: {So, on the whole, I'd say} it depends on what you're studying.

ex.q: Will life be better or worse in fifty years?
ex.t: {So, on the whole, I'd say} better, as long as we look after the planet.

reels.p: What do you think, …? / I agree with what … said about …
reels.bt: What do you think, Tomás? I agree with what Inês said about…
reels.note: Part 4 is three people talking. Hand it back, or pick up what your partner said.

ex.q: Why is fast food so popular?
ex.t: Mostly because it's quick and cheap. {What do you think,} Tomás?

ex.scene: Tomás has just said that footballers are paid far too much.
ex.t: {I agree with what} Tomás {said about} footballers. Nurses deserve that money more.

ex.scene: Inês has just said that teenagers and parents rarely understand each other.
ex.t: {I agree with what} Inês {said about} parents, but I think it's getting better.
